intro: At B1 you learnt the words for getting a job: vacancy, CV, interview, salary, promotion. Now you've got the job, so let's talk about the work itself: **meetings, projects and deadlines**, the **money** (budget, revenue, costs, profit) and **who does what** in a company (department, team lead, report to). Warm-up: how many meetings do you have in a normal week?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in three themed groups with an Indonesian gloss and practise them in short, natural sentences with Indonesian work contexts (a startup in Jakarta, a BUMN = state-owned company, an e-commerce company, an online shop in Solo, KPI, rupiah). Recap in one line, don't reteach: from a2-vocab-work-study the learner knows meeting, report, deadline, colleague, manager, office, shift; from b1-vocab-work-education the job-hunting words (apply for, vacancy, CV, cover letter, interview, hire, salary, internship, promotion, resign); from b1-phrasal-verbs put off, call off, set up. Don't repeat the careers/CV vocabulary.

Meetings, projects and deadlines: agenda (the list of topics for one meeting; Indonesian 'agenda saya padat' = my schedule is busy, so steer 'agenda' to meetings), brief someone (on something) = give them the key facts before they start (a briefing), discuss + the topic directly, take the minutes (notulen; always plural, nothing to do with time), action points (UK; US action items: tasks with a name and a deadline), follow up (on something / with someone; noun a follow-up, with a hyphen), postpone (= a formal put off: move to later) vs cancel (no meeting at all; UK cancelled, US canceled), stakeholder, milestone, deliverable, on track / on schedule, behind schedule, ahead of schedule, meet / miss a deadline (verb-noun collocations are taught in depth in b2-collocations: just use them). KPI = key performance indicator, plural KPIs. Common error: *'We need to discuss about the budget' (from mendiskusikan tentang / membahas tentang): discuss takes the topic directly; talk ABOUT and the noun a discussion ABOUT are correct, so never mark those wrong.

Basic finance: revenue − costs = profit. revenue (pendapatan, omzet: all the money from sales), costs (biaya), expenses (pengeluaran, especially staff spending the company pays back: claim expenses; Indonesians say 'reimburse'), profit (laba/untung), loss (rugi), break even (impas, balik modal; past broke even), budget (anggaran; over budget, within budget), invoice (tagihan/faktur, sent BEFORE payment) vs receipt (kuitansi, AFTER payment), quarter (Q1 = first quarter, usually January–March, though some companies' financial year starts in another month), increase / decrease by + amount (naik sebesar), an increase in + thing; stress usually IN-crease (noun) vs in-CREASE (verb). Common error: *'The company got a big profit' (from mendapat untung) → made a profit; 'earn a profit' and American 'turn a profit' are also correct. make a loss is mainly British (Americans often say lose money). income = a person's penghasilan; in company reports 'net income' means profit, so use revenue for sales money. IMPORTANT: revenue/income/sales and cost/expense overlap: never make them compete as options in one question; test clear meanings (revenue vs profit vs budget) and clear collocations (make a profit, break even, increase by).

Roles and structure: department (Indonesian offices say 'divisi'; in English a division is usually a much bigger part of a large company, so teach department or 'I work in Finance'), head of + department (Head of Finance), manager, team lead (tech / American) / team leader (British), report to someone = that person is your boss (I report to Bu Ani = Bu Ani atasan saya; keep the question 'Who do you report to?' for the checkpoint, don't model it in practice), be responsible for (bertanggung jawab atas) the work or the people you look after, be in charge of (memimpin, memegang), colleague (rekan kerja, same organisation) vs counterpart (same job in another organisation or office). Direktur Utama in a BUMN = CEO / President Director. staff is usually the whole group (20 staff, a member of staff / a staff member; not 'she's a staff'). Common error: *'I am responsible to the marketing team' → responsible for. ('responsible to' exists as a rare formal phrase meaning answerable to a person or body: don't teach it.) responsible for and in charge of mean almost the same: never make them compete. 'colleague' is sometimes used loosely for people in the same profession, so don't mark it wrong in free answers; teach counterpart as the precise word.

Limits: A0–B1 grammar only (present simple and continuous, past simple, present perfect, will / going to, first and second conditionals, can / should / have to, present and past simple passive, defining relative clauses, gerunds and infinitives, reported statements). No third conditional, wish, past modals (must have), participle clauses, non-defining relative clauses, causative or future perfect. Don't teach accounting (gross vs net profit, cash flow, balance sheet, EBITDA) beyond what's above, idioms (that's b2-phrasal-verbs-idioms) or formal email register (b2-formal-informal-vocab). Correct one thing at a time, usually discuss about, got a profit or responsible to.

keyPoints.title: Meetings, projects and deadlines
keyPoints.explanation: Before a meeting you read the agenda (the list of topics), and someone may brief you (give you the key facts). In the meeting you discuss the topics (discuss + topic, no 'about'), and someone takes the minutes (the written record). At the end there are action points, and later you follow up. A project has stakeholders, milestones and deliverables, and it is on track, behind schedule or ahead of schedule. Postpone = move to a later time; cancel = no meeting at all.

examples.en: Please read the agenda before Monday's meeting.
examples.id: Tolong baca agenda rapatnya sebelum rapat hari Senin.

examples.en: We discussed the new KPIs for over an hour.
examples.id: Kami membahas KPI baru itu lebih dari satu jam.

examples.en: We're two weeks behind schedule because the designer was ill.
examples.id: Kami terlambat dua minggu dari jadwal karena desainernya sakit.

id.title: Rapat, proyek dan tenggat
id.explanation: Sebelum rapat kamu membaca agenda (daftar topiknya), dan seseorang mungkin brief kamu (memberi info pentingnya secara singkat). Dalam rapat kamu discuss topiknya (discuss + topik, tanpa 'about'), dan seseorang takes the minutes (mencatat notulen). Di akhir ada action points (poin tindak lanjut), dan nanti kamu follow up (menindaklanjuti). Sebuah proyek punya stakeholders (pemangku kepentingan), milestones (tahap penting) dan deliverables (hasil kerja yang diserahkan), dan proyeknya bisa on track (sesuai rencana), behind schedule (terlambat dari jadwal) atau ahead of schedule (lebih cepat dari jadwal). Postpone = menunda ke waktu lain; cancel = membatalkan, rapatnya tidak jadi sama sekali.

keyPoints.title: Money: revenue − costs = profit
keyPoints.explanation: Revenue is all the money from sales; costs are the money you spend; profit is what's left. You make a profit (not 'get a profit'), make a loss, or break even (revenue = costs). A budget is the money you plan to spend; an invoice asks for payment; a quarter (Q1–Q4) is three months. Numbers increase or decrease by an amount: Revenue increased by 20%.

examples.en: Our revenue increased by 20% in Q3.
examples.id: Pendapatan kami naik sebesar 20% di kuartal ketiga.

examples.en: The shop made a profit of Rp50 million last year.
examples.id: Toko itu mendapat laba Rp50 juta tahun lalu.

examples.en: We need to cut costs: the project is over budget.
examples.id: Kita perlu memangkas biaya: proyeknya melebihi anggaran.

id.title: Uang: revenue − costs = profit
id.explanation: Revenue (pendapatan, omzet) adalah semua uang dari penjualan; costs (biaya) adalah uang yang kamu keluarkan; profit (laba) adalah sisanya. Kamu make a profit (bukan 'get a profit'), make a loss (rugi), atau break even (impas: revenue = costs). Budget (anggaran) adalah uang yang kamu rencanakan untuk dibelanjakan; invoice (tagihan) meminta pembayaran; quarter (kuartal, Q1–Q4) adalah tiga bulan. Angka increase (naik) atau decrease (turun) by (sebesar) suatu jumlah: Revenue increased by 20%.

keyPoints.title: Roles and structure: who does what
keyPoints.explanation: A company has departments, each with a head of department; a team lead runs a small team. You report to your boss, you are responsible for (not 'to') your work or your team, and someone is in charge of each project. A colleague works in your own organisation; your counterpart has the same job as you in another organisation.

examples.en: All the team leads report to Pak Hasan, the Head of IT.
examples.id: Semua ketua tim melapor kepada Pak Hasan, Kepala TI.

examples.en: Rina is responsible for the company's Instagram account.
examples.id: Rina bertanggung jawab atas akun Instagram perusahaan.

examples.en: I'm meeting my counterpart from our partner company in Malaysia.
examples.id: Saya akan bertemu mitra sejawat saya dari perusahaan mitra kami di Malaysia.

id.title: Peran dan struktur: siapa melakukan apa
id.explanation: Perusahaan punya departments (departemen, divisi), masing-masing dengan head of department (kepala departemen); team lead (ketua tim) memimpin tim kecil. Kamu report to (melapor kepada) atasanmu, kamu responsible for (bukan 'to') pekerjaan atau timmu, dan ada orang yang in charge of (memegang) setiap proyek. Colleague (rekan kerja) bekerja di organisasimu sendiri; counterpart (mitra sejawat) punya pekerjaan yang sama denganmu di organisasi lain.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: At the end of the meeting, Pak Hasan read out the action ___: who has to do what, and by when.
guidedPractice.hint: The tasks from a meeting, each with a name and a deadline: action ___ (British), action items (American).

guidedPractice.hint: The list of topics for one meeting, often sent a day or two before.

Complete with one word: Our revenue increased ___ 12% in the second quarter.
guidedPractice.hint: naik sebesar 12% → increased ___ 12%. With the noun you'd say an increase of 12%.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: Pak Hasan is ___ charge of the new project in Bandung.
guidedPractice.hint: The phrase is be ___ charge of (memimpin, memegang).

independentPractice.prompt: Your team is going to finish the report three days after the deadline. Tell your manager in one short sentence, using behind schedule.
expected: we are three days behind schedule
the report is three days behind schedule
independentPractice.hint: Subject + be + behind schedule: We're … behind schedule.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: The startup sent the client an ___ for Rp15 million. The client has to pay within 30 days.
independentPractice.hint: The document a seller sends to ask for payment (tagihan, faktur). After you pay, you get a receipt.

independentPractice.prompt: Rina works in the HR department. Complete with one word: Rina is responsible ___ hiring new staff.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Let's discuss about the launch date in Monday's meeting.
acceptableAnswers: let's discuss the launch date in monday's meeting
lets discuss the launch date in mondays meeting
let's discuss the launch date at monday's meeting
lets discuss the launch date at mondays meeting
let us discuss the launch date in monday's meeting
let us discuss the launch date at monday's meeting
let's talk about the launch date in monday's meeting
let's talk about the launch date at monday's meeting
lets talk about the launch date in mondays meeting
let's have a discussion about the launch date in monday's meeting
assessment.rubric: Correct: Let's discuss the launch date in (or at) Monday's meeting: discuss takes the topic directly, with no 'about' (the node's common error, from mendiskusikan tentang). 'Let's talk about the launch date …' = 100 (talk needs about). 'Let's discuss on the launch date' = 20 (still an extra word). Unchanged 'discuss about' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Read Sari's message to her team: 'Hi all, Pak Hasan is ill today, so we can't have the project meeting at 2 p.m. We'll have it next Tuesday at 2 instead. Sorry for the change!' Complete with one verb in the past: Sari ___ the meeting until next Tuesday.
acceptableAnswers: postponed
put off
assessment.rubric: Correct: postponed (the meeting will still happen, but later; put off is the less formal phrasal verb and also 100). 'delayed' = 70 (the right idea, but we usually postpone a meeting). 'rescheduled' = 70 (the right idea, but it goes with for/to: rescheduled it for next Tuesday). 'cancelled' / 'canceled' = 0 (cancel means there is no meeting at all). 'postpone' = 60 (right word, not in the past).

assessment.prompt: In the second quarter, a café in Bandung had revenue of Rp300 million, but its costs were Rp340 million. Complete with one word: In Q2, the café made a ___ of Rp40 million.
acceptableAnswers: loss
assessment.rubric: Correct: loss (costs were bigger than revenue: 300 − 340 = −40, so the café lost Rp40 million). 'profit' = 0 (the sign is the wrong way round). 'lost' = 30 (right idea, but 'made a lost' isn't English: the noun is loss). 'deficit' = 50 (understandable, but we make a loss).

assessment.prompt: A food delivery startup in Surabaya had revenue of Rp2 billion last year, and its costs were also Rp2 billion: no profit and no loss. Complete with two words in the past: Last year, the startup ___ ___.
acceptableAnswers: broke even
assessment.rubric: Correct: broke even (revenue = costs: impas, balik modal; break is irregular: break – broke – broken). 'break even' = 60 (right phrase, but not in the past). 'breaked even' = 50 (right phrase, wrong past form). 'broken even' = 50. 'made nothing' or 'made no profit' = 40 (true, but not the expression).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Our online shop got a profit for the first time last year.
acceptableAnswers: our online shop made a profit for the first time last year
our online shop made a profit last year for the first time
last year our online shop made a profit for the first time
our online shop made its first profit last year
our online shop earned a profit for the first time last year
our online shop turned a profit for the first time last year
assessment.rubric: Correct: Our online shop made a profit for the first time last year (make a profit, not 'get a profit': the node's common error, from mendapat untung). 'earned a profit' and 'turned a profit' (American) = 100. 'Our online shop was profitable for the first time last year' = 90 (correct, but changes the structure). 'did a profit' = 0. Unchanged 'got a profit' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Bu Ani leads the finance team at a BUMN in Jakarta. Correct the mistake: Bu Ani is responsible to the finance team.
acceptableAnswers: bu ani is responsible for the finance team
bu ani's responsible for the finance team
bu ani is in charge of the finance team
bu ani is the head of the finance team
bu ani is head of the finance team
assessment.rubric: Correct: Bu Ani is responsible for the finance team (be responsible FOR the work or the people you look after: the node's common error). 'Bu Ani is in charge of the finance team' or '… the head of the finance team' = 100. 'responsible of' = 20. Unchanged 'responsible to' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Budi has just joined an e-commerce company in Jakarta. On his first day, he wants to know who his new colleague's boss is. Complete his question with two words: Who do you ___ ___?
acceptableAnswers: report to
answer to
assessment.rubric: Correct: report to (Who do you report to? = Siapa atasanmu?). 'answer to' = 100 (same meaning, less common). 'work under' = 80 (understood, but report to is the usual phrase). 'work for' = 30 ('Who do you work for?' usually asks which company). 'report' alone = 50 (the to is needed).

blocks.text:
Quick recap: from A2 and B1 you know **meeting**, **deadline**, **colleague**, **manager** and *put off* (menunda). Now the words around a meeting, in the order they happen:
- **Before:** the **agenda** (daftar topik rapat) is the list of topics, often sent a day or two before: *Item 3 on the agenda is the budget.* You **brief** someone (memberi penjelasan singkat) when you tell them the key facts before they start: *Can you brief me on the project before the call?* A short meeting like that is **a briefing**.
- **During:** you **discuss** the topics (membahas). Someone **takes the minutes** (mencatat notulen). **The minutes** = the written record of what people decided. It always has *-s*, and here it has nothing to do with time.
- **At the end:** **action points** (poin tindak lanjut) are the tasks, each with a name and a deadline. Americans often say **action items**.
- **After:** you **follow up** (menindaklanjuti): *I'll follow up on the action points. I'll follow up with the client.* The noun has a hyphen: *a follow-up email*.

You'll also hear **KPI** (said 'kay-pee-eye') = key performance indicator (indikator kinerja utama): a number target for a person or a team. Plural: *KPIs*.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: dari A2 dan B1 kamu sudah tahu **meeting**, **deadline**, **colleague**, **manager** dan *put off* (menunda). Sekarang kata-kata seputar rapat, sesuai urutan kejadiannya:
- **Sebelum:** **agenda** (daftar topik rapat) adalah daftar topiknya, sering dikirim sehari atau dua hari sebelumnya: *Item 3 on the agenda is the budget.* Kamu **brief** seseorang (memberi penjelasan singkat) saat kamu memberi tahu info pentingnya sebelum dia mulai: *Can you brief me on the project before the call?* Rapat singkat seperti itu disebut **a briefing**.
- **Selama rapat:** kamu **discuss** topiknya (membahas). Seseorang **takes the minutes** (mencatat notulen). **The minutes** = catatan tertulis tentang apa yang diputuskan. Kata ini selalu pakai *-s*, dan di sini tidak ada hubungannya dengan waktu (menit).
- **Di akhir:** **action points** (poin tindak lanjut) adalah tugas-tugasnya, masing-masing dengan nama orang dan tenggat. Orang Amerika sering bilang **action items**.
- **Sesudahnya:** kamu **follow up** (menindaklanjuti): *I'll follow up on the action points. I'll follow up with the client.* Kata bendanya pakai tanda hubung: *a follow-up email*.

Kamu juga akan mendengar **KPI** (dibaca 'kei-pi-ai') = key performance indicator (indikator kinerja utama): target angka untuk seseorang atau sebuah tim. Bentuk jamaknya: *KPIs*.

blocks.text:
Two Indonesian traps:
- **discuss has no 'about'.** *mendiskusikan tentang / membahas tentang* → `We need to discuss about the budget` ✗. Say **We need to discuss the budget**: discuss + the topic directly. But **talk about** and the noun **a discussion about** do take *about*: *Let's talk about the budget. We had a long discussion about it.*
- **agenda is not your day.** In Indonesian, *agenda saya padat* means your day is full. In English an **agenda** is usually the list of topics for a meeting (*What's on the agenda?*). For your day, say *I have a busy schedule today* or *I'm busy all day*.

id.text:
Dua jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:
- **discuss tidak pakai 'about'.** *mendiskusikan tentang / membahas tentang* → `We need to discuss about the budget` ✗. Katakan **We need to discuss the budget**: discuss + topiknya langsung. Tapi **talk about** dan kata benda **a discussion about** memang pakai *about*: *Let's talk about the budget. We had a long discussion about it.*
- **agenda bukan jadwal harianmu.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *agenda saya padat* berarti harimu penuh. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **agenda** biasanya daftar topik untuk sebuah rapat (*What's on the agenda?*). Untuk harimu, katakan *I have a busy schedule today* atau *I'm busy all day*.

blocks.prompt: After the meeting, Dimas writes a short record of what everyone decided and emails it to the team. What is he doing?
blocks.explain: A written record of what people decided in a meeting is **the minutes** (notulen), so Dimas is **taking the minutes**. The **agenda** comes before the meeting (the list of topics), and **briefing** someone means giving them the key facts before they start.

id.prompt: Setelah rapat, Dimas menulis catatan singkat tentang apa yang diputuskan semua orang dan mengirimkannya lewat email ke timnya. Apa yang sedang dia lakukan?
id.explain: Catatan tertulis tentang apa yang diputuskan dalam rapat disebut **the minutes** (notulen), jadi Dimas sedang **taking the minutes**. **Agenda** dibuat sebelum rapat (daftar topiknya), dan **briefing** seseorang berarti memberi info pentingnya sebelum dia mulai.

blocks.text:
A project has **stakeholders** (pemangku kepentingan): everyone who cares about the result, like the client, your manager, the users or the investors. The big steps on the way are **milestones** (tahap penting): *The first milestone is a working app by June.* The things you have to hand over are the **deliverables** (hasil kerja yang harus diserahkan): a report, a design, an app.

How is it going?
- **on track** / **on schedule** = sesuai rencana / sesuai jadwal
- **behind schedule** = terlambat dari jadwal
- **ahead of schedule** = lebih cepat dari jadwal
- you **meet** a deadline (selesai tepat waktu) or **miss** it (terlewat)

Changing a meeting or an event:
- **postpone** (menunda, mengundur) = move it to a later time. It's a more formal *put off*: *We postponed the launch until July.*
- **cancel** (membatalkan) = it won't happen at all.

id.text:
Sebuah proyek punya **stakeholders** (pemangku kepentingan): semua orang yang peduli pada hasilnya, misalnya klien, manajermu, para pengguna atau investor. Langkah-langkah besar di perjalanannya disebut **milestones** (tahap penting): *The first milestone is a working app by June.* Hal-hal yang harus kamu serahkan disebut **deliverables** (hasil kerja yang harus diserahkan): laporan, desain, aplikasi.

Bagaimana perkembangannya?
- **on track** / **on schedule** = sesuai rencana / sesuai jadwal
- **behind schedule** = terlambat dari jadwal
- **ahead of schedule** = lebih cepat dari jadwal
- kamu **meet** a deadline (selesai tepat waktu) atau **miss** it (terlewat)

Mengubah rapat atau acara:
- **postpone** (menunda, mengundur) = memindahkannya ke waktu yang lebih nanti. Ini versi lebih formal dari *put off*: *We postponed the launch until July.*
- **cancel** (membatalkan) = acaranya tidak jadi sama sekali.

rows.en: The project is on track: we reached the first milestone last week.
rows.id: Proyeknya sesuai rencana: kami mencapai tahap penting pertama minggu lalu.

rows.en: We're two weeks behind schedule because the designer was ill.
rows.id: Kami terlambat dua minggu dari jadwal karena desainernya sakit.

rows.en: The client is our most important stakeholder.
rows.id: Klien adalah pemangku kepentingan kami yang paling penting.

rows.en: The deliverables are a final report and a short video.
rows.id: Hasil kerja yang harus diserahkan adalah laporan akhir dan video pendek.

rows.en: The training was postponed to next month.
rows.id: Pelatihannya diundur ke bulan depan.
rows.note: postponed = it will still happen, later

rows.en: If we miss the deadline, the client won't be happy.
rows.id: Kalau kita melewatkan tenggatnya, kliennya tidak akan senang.

blocks.text:
**postpone or cancel?** *ditunda* or *diundur* = **postponed** (it will happen later). *dibatalkan* = **cancelled** (it won't happen). Spelling: British *cancelled*, American *canceled*.

**schedule** sounds different: many British speakers say 'SHED-yool', Americans say 'SKED-jool'. Both are fine.

id.text:
**postpone atau cancel?** *ditunda* atau *diundur* = **postponed** (tetap terjadi, nanti). *dibatalkan* = **cancelled** (tidak jadi). Ejaannya: British *cancelled*, Amerika *canceled*.

**schedule** dibaca berbeda: banyak penutur British bilang 'SYED-yuul', orang Amerika bilang 'SKED-juul'. Dua-duanya benar.

blocks.prompt: The team finished the new website a week before the deadline. The project is ___.
blocks.explain: They finished **before** the deadline, so the project is **ahead of schedule** (lebih cepat dari jadwal). *behind schedule* means late, and *postponed* means moved to a later time.

id.prompt: Timnya menyelesaikan website baru seminggu sebelum tenggat. Lengkapi: The project is ___.
id.explain: Mereka selesai **sebelum** tenggat, jadi proyeknya **ahead of schedule** (lebih cepat dari jadwal). *behind schedule* berarti terlambat, dan *postponed* berarti dipindah ke waktu yang lebih nanti.

blocks.text:
The sum every business knows:
**revenue − costs = profit** (pendapatan − biaya = laba)
- **revenue** (pendapatan, *omzet*): all the money that comes in from sales.
- **costs** (biaya): the money you spend to run the business: salaries, rent, ads. Staff also have **expenses** (pengeluaran untuk kerja, like travel): you **claim your expenses** and the company pays you back (what Indonesian offices call *reimburse*).
- **profit** (laba, untung): what's left. If costs are bigger than revenue, you have a **loss** (rugi). If revenue and costs are the same, you **break even** (impas, balik modal). *break* is irregular: past **broke even**.
- **budget** (anggaran): the money you plan to spend: *over budget* (melebihi anggaran), *within budget*.
- **invoice** (tagihan, faktur): what a seller sends to ask for payment. After you pay, you get a **receipt** (kuitansi, bukti bayar).
- **quarter** (kuartal): three months. **Q1** = the first quarter, usually January to March (some companies start their financial year in another month).
- **increase / decrease** (naik / turun) are verbs and nouns: *Revenue increased **by** 15%* (naik sebesar 15%), *an increase **in** sales*. Stress: the noun is usually **IN**-crease, the verb in-**CREASE**.

id.text:
Rumus yang diketahui setiap bisnis:
**revenue − costs = profit** (pendapatan − biaya = laba)
- **revenue** (pendapatan, *omzet*): semua uang yang masuk dari penjualan.
- **costs** (biaya): uang yang kamu keluarkan untuk menjalankan bisnis: gaji, sewa, iklan. Karyawan juga punya **expenses** (pengeluaran untuk kerja, misalnya perjalanan dinas): kamu **claim your expenses** dan perusahaan menggantinya (yang di kantor Indonesia disebut *reimburse*).
- **profit** (laba, untung): sisanya. Kalau biaya lebih besar dari pendapatan, kamu mengalami **loss** (rugi). Kalau pendapatan dan biaya sama, kamu **break even** (impas, balik modal). *break* itu tidak beraturan: bentuk lampaunya **broke even**.
- **budget** (anggaran): uang yang kamu rencanakan untuk dibelanjakan: *over budget* (melebihi anggaran), *within budget* (sesuai anggaran).
- **invoice** (tagihan, faktur): yang dikirim penjual untuk meminta pembayaran. Setelah kamu bayar, kamu dapat **receipt** (kuitansi, bukti bayar).
- **quarter** (kuartal): tiga bulan. **Q1** = kuartal pertama, biasanya Januari sampai Maret (ada perusahaan yang tahun bukunya mulai di bulan lain).
- **increase / decrease** (naik / turun) bisa jadi kata kerja maupun kata benda: *Revenue increased **by** 15%* (naik sebesar 15%), *an increase **in** sales* (kenaikan penjualan). Tekanannya: kata benda biasanya **IN**-crease, kata kerja in-**CREASE**.

rows.en: Our revenue increased by 20% in Q3.
rows.id: Pendapatan kami naik sebesar 20% di kuartal ketiga.

rows.en: We need to cut costs: the project is over budget.
rows.id: Kita perlu memangkas biaya: proyeknya melebihi anggaran.

rows.en: The shop made a profit of Rp50 million last year.
rows.id: Toko itu mendapat laba Rp50 juta tahun lalu.
rows.note: make a profit, not 'get a profit'

id.note: make a profit, bukan 'get a profit'

rows.en: The new branch in Bandung broke even after six months.
rows.id: Cabang baru di Bandung balik modal setelah enam bulan.

rows.en: Please send the invoice to our finance department.

rows.en: Keep your receipts if you want to claim your travel expenses.
rows.id: Simpan kuitansimu kalau kamu mau mengajukan penggantian biaya perjalanan.

blocks.text:
Three traps:
- **make a profit**, not 'get a profit' (from *mendapat untung*): `The company got a big profit` ✗ → *The company made a big profit.* The opposite is **make a loss** (British; Americans more often say *lose money*).
- **revenue or income?** For a person, **income** is *penghasilan* (*my monthly income*). For a company, the money from sales is **revenue**. In company reports *net income* means the profit after everything, so don't use *income* for sales.
- **costs and expenses** mean almost the same. Just learn the usual phrases: *cut costs* (memangkas biaya), *running costs* (biaya operasional), *travel expenses*, *claim expenses*.

id.text:
Tiga jebakan:
- **make a profit**, bukan 'get a profit' (dari *mendapat untung*): `The company got a big profit` ✗ → *The company made a big profit.* Lawannya **make a loss** (British; orang Amerika lebih sering bilang *lose money*).
- **revenue atau income?** Untuk orang, **income** adalah *penghasilan* (*my monthly income*). Untuk perusahaan, uang dari penjualan adalah **revenue**. Dalam laporan perusahaan, *net income* berarti laba setelah semuanya dikurangi, jadi jangan pakai *income* untuk penjualan.
- **costs dan expenses** artinya hampir sama. Hafalkan saja frasa yang biasa dipakai: *cut costs* (memangkas biaya), *running costs* (biaya operasional), *travel expenses* (biaya perjalanan), *claim expenses* (mengajukan penggantian biaya).

options: The café got a profit last month.
The café did a profit last month.
The café made a profit last month.
blocks.explain: The verb with profit and loss is **make**: *make a profit, make a loss*. 'got a profit' is a word-for-word translation of *mendapat untung*, and 'did a profit' isn't English.

id.explain: Kata kerja untuk profit dan loss adalah **make**: *make a profit, make a loss*. 'got a profit' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *mendapat untung*, dan 'did a profit' bukan bahasa Inggris.

material.title: Who does what: roles and structure

blocks.text:
A company is split into **departments** (departemen): *the finance department, HR, marketing, IT*. Indonesian offices often say *divisi*, but in English a **division** is usually a much bigger part of a large company. For your part of the office, say **department**, or just *I work in Finance*.
- **head of** + department (kepala): *Bu Ani is the Head of Finance.*
- **manager** (manajer) and **team lead / team leader** (ketua tim). *team lead* is common in tech companies and American English; *team leader* is more British.
- **report to** someone = that person is your direct boss (atasan langsung): *I report to the Head of Sales.*
- **be responsible for** something or someone (bertanggung jawab atas): *She's responsible for the budget.* **be in charge of** (memimpin, memegang) means almost the same: *Who's in charge of the event?*
- **colleague** (rekan kerja): someone in your own organisation. **counterpart** (mitra sejawat): someone who has the same job as you in **another** organisation or office: *my counterpart at the partner bank*.
- In a BUMN (a **state-owned company**), the *Direktur Utama* is called the **CEO** or **President Director** in English.

id.text:
Sebuah perusahaan dibagi menjadi **departments** (departemen): *the finance department, HR, marketing, IT*. Kantor di Indonesia sering bilang *divisi*, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris **division** biasanya bagian yang jauh lebih besar dari perusahaan besar. Untuk bagianmu di kantor, katakan **department**, atau cukup *I work in Finance*.
- **head of** + departemen (kepala): *Bu Ani is the Head of Finance.*
- **manager** (manajer) dan **team lead / team leader** (ketua tim). *team lead* umum di perusahaan teknologi dan bahasa Inggris Amerika; *team leader* lebih British.
- **report to** seseorang = orang itu atasan langsungmu: *I report to the Head of Sales.*
- **be responsible for** sesuatu atau seseorang (bertanggung jawab atas): *She's responsible for the budget.* **be in charge of** (memimpin, memegang) artinya hampir sama: *Who's in charge of the event?*
- **colleague** (rekan kerja): orang di organisasimu sendiri. **counterpart** (mitra sejawat): orang yang pekerjaannya sama denganmu di organisasi atau kantor **lain**: *my counterpart at the partner bank*.
- Di BUMN (**state-owned company**, perusahaan milik negara), *Direktur Utama* dalam bahasa Inggris disebut **CEO** atau **President Director**.

rows.en: Sari works in the HR department of a BUMN.
rows.id: Sari bekerja di departemen SDM sebuah BUMN.

rows.en: Dimas is the team lead for the mobile app.
rows.id: Dimas adalah ketua tim untuk aplikasi mobile.

rows.en: All the team leads report to Pak Hasan, the Head of IT.
rows.id: Semua ketua tim melapor kepada Pak Hasan, Kepala TI.
rows.note: report to = he is their boss

rows.en: Rina is responsible for the company's Instagram account.
rows.id: Rina bertanggung jawab atas akun Instagram perusahaan.

rows.en: Who's in charge of the office party this year?
rows.id: Siapa yang memegang acara pesta kantor tahun ini?

rows.en: I'm meeting my counterpart from our partner company in Malaysia.
rows.id: Saya akan bertemu mitra sejawat saya dari perusahaan mitra kami di Malaysia.
rows.note: counterpart = the same job, in another organisation

id.note: counterpart = pekerjaan yang sama, di organisasi lain

blocks.text:
Indonesian traps:
- **responsible for**, not 'responsible to': `I am responsible to the marketing team` ✗ → *I am responsible **for** the marketing team.* For the work or the people you look after, always use **for**.
- **report to** is about your boss, not just *lapor*: *Sari reports to Bu Ani* = Bu Ani atasan langsung Sari.
- **staff** usually means the whole group: *We have 20 staff.* For one person, say *a member of staff* or *a staff member*, not 'she's a staff'.

id.text:
Jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:
- **responsible for**, bukan 'responsible to': `I am responsible to the marketing team` ✗ → *I am responsible **for** the marketing team.* Untuk pekerjaan atau orang yang kamu urus, selalu pakai **for**.
- **report to** itu tentang atasanmu, bukan sekadar *lapor*: *Sari reports to Bu Ani* = Bu Ani atasan langsung Sari.
- **staff** biasanya berarti seluruh kelompok karyawan: *We have 20 staff.* Untuk satu orang, katakan *a member of staff* atau *a staff member*, bukan 'she's a staff'.

blocks.explain: Someone in your own organisation is a **colleague** (rekan kerja). A **counterpart** has the same job as you in a **different** organisation or office.

id.explain: Orang di organisasimu sendiri adalah **colleague** (rekan kerja). **Counterpart** punya pekerjaan yang sama denganmu di organisasi atau kantor yang **berbeda**.

id.intro: Di B1 kamu sudah belajar kata-kata untuk mencari kerja: vacancy, CV, interview, salary, promotion. Sekarang kamu sudah dapat pekerjaannya, jadi ayo bicara tentang pekerjaannya sendiri: **rapat, proyek dan tenggat**, soal **uang** (budget, revenue, costs, profit) dan **siapa melakukan apa** di perusahaan (department, team lead, report to).
